message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **Halloween** | John Carpenter | The original slasher that set the template for the genre. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | A psychological horror masterpiece based on Stephen King’s novel. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | Wes Craven | Introduces Freddy Krueger, blending dream logic with visceral scares. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | Jonathan Demme | A tense thriller featuring Hannibal Lecter and Clarice Starling. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** | Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez | Pioneered found‑footage horror, creating a sense of realism. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | Revitalized zombie horror with a fast‑moving, post‑apocalyptic vibe. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan & Leigh Whannell | Introduced a new kind of psychological horror with intricate traps. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage film that sparked a whole franchise. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | Combines supernatural elements with a grounded investigative approach. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | A meta‑take on horror tropes that subverts expectations. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | A fresh take on a supernatural curse with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | A slow‑burn period horror that builds dread through atmosphere. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | A socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine scares. |
| 2018 | **Hereditary** | Ari Aster | A deeply unsettling film that explores grief and family trauma. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that turns a pastoral setting into a nightmare. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling of the classic story with a strong female lead. |
| 2021 | **A Quiet Place Part II** | John Krasinski | Builds on the tension of silence and sound‑based horror. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** | Scott Derrickson | A supernatural thriller that mixes folklore with modern horror. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | Gerard Johnstone | A horror‑comedy about a murderous AI doll that feels eerily relevant. |

Feel free to pick any from the list that match your mood—whether you’re after a classic slash‑and‑dice vibe or something more psychological and atmospheric. Happy watching!
